title: "How Social Media Influencers Build Brand Loyalty Among Millennial Consumers"

# --- Mode: manuscript (the default) or article (a publication-style
#     preview for sharing drafts; PDF and .tex only) ---
jcp-mode: manuscript

jcp-article-type: article

# --- Abstract (at most 175 words) ---
abstract: |
  Social media has changed the way brands connect with consumers, and many
  brands now work with social media influencers to reach their target
  audiences. This research investigates the role of influencers in building
  brand loyalty among millennial consumers. A survey of 200 consumers shows
  that trust in an influencer is positively associated with loyalty to the
  brands the influencer endorses, and that this association is stronger for
  familiar brands. The research offers guidance on how brands can work with
  influencers to strengthen their relationships with consumers.

keywords:
  - social media
  - influencers
  - brand loyalty
  - millennial consumers

bibliography: bibliography.bib

Social media has become an essential part of daily life, and it has changed
the way consumers present themselves and connect with one another
[@belk2013]. It has also changed the way brands connect with consumers. Many
brands now work with social media influencers to reach and engage their
target audiences.

# Theoretical Background

Brand loyalty represents the degree to which customers are committed to
purchasing a particular brand, and it is a central component of brand equity
[@aaker1991]. Research on relationship marketing in consumer markets
[@bagozzi1995] suggests that consumers form relationships with
brands.[^fn1]

[^fn1]: Use footnotes sparingly. JCP presents them on a separate page at the
end of the article.

## Social Media Influencers and Brand Loyalty

Influencers can strengthen brand loyalty by providing valuable content and
by engaging with their followers. Internet-enabled market environments
change how firms build and defend their positions [@varadarajan2008], and
influencers have become part of that environment.

::: {.hypothesis}
H1: Trust in an influencer is positively associated with loyalty to the
brands that the influencer endorses.
:::

::: {.hypothesis}
H2: The association between trust in an influencer and brand loyalty is
stronger for familiar brands than for unfamiliar brands.
:::

# Method

## Participants and Design

Two hundred members of an online panel completed the survey. Participants
rated their trust in an influencer they follow, their familiarity with a
brand the influencer endorses, and their loyalty to that brand.

## Measures

### Brand Loyalty

Four items measured brand loyalty on 7-point scales.

### Influencer Trust

Three items measured trust in the influencer on 7-point scales. We
evaluated the measurement model with the criteria that @bagozzi1988
recommend. @tbl-descriptives reports descriptive statistics.

| Variable         | *M*  | *SD* | *n* |
|:-----------------|-----:|-----:|----:|
| Brand loyalty^a^ | 4.21 | 1.02 | 200 |
| Purchase intent  | 3.87 | 1.15 | 200 |
| Influencer trust | 4.56 | 0.89 | 200 |

: Descriptive statistics for the study variables {#tbl-descriptives}

::: {.notes}
All variables were measured on 7-point scales.

^a^Average of four items.
:::

# Results

@eq-model presents the model:

$$
\mathit{Loyalty}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \mathit{Trust}_i + \beta_2 \mathit{Familiarity}_i + \beta_3 \mathit{Trust}_i \times \mathit{Familiarity}_i + \varepsilon_i
$$ {#eq-model}

Trust in the influencer was positively associated with brand loyalty,
*b* = 0.38, *SE* = 0.08, *p* < .001, and this association was stronger for
familiar brands, *b* = 0.15, *SE* = 0.06, *p* = .013 (@tbl-regression and
@fig-loyalty).

| Predictor              | Model 1     | Model 2     |
|:-----------------------|:-----------:|:-----------:|
| Intercept              | 2.45 (0.21) | 2.31 (0.20) |
| Influencer trust       | 0.42 (0.08) | 0.38 (0.08) |
| Brand familiarity      | 0.28 (0.07) | 0.25 (0.07) |
| Trust × Familiarity    |             | 0.15 (0.06) |
| *R*^2^                 | .31         | .34         |

: Regression of brand loyalty on influencer trust and brand familiarity {#tbl-regression}

::: {.notes}
Unstandardized coefficients, with standard errors in parentheses.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-loyalty
#| fig-cap: "Brand loyalty by trust in the influencer and brand familiarity. Error bars represent ±1 *SE*"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.6

library(ggplot2)

# Estimated means and standard errors from Model 2
loyalty <- data.frame(
  trust = factor(rep(c("Low trust", "High trust"), times = 2),
                 levels = c("Low trust", "High trust")),
  familiarity = rep(c("Unfamiliar brand", "Familiar brand"), each = 2),
  mean = c(3.62, 4.05, 3.80, 4.88),
  se = c(0.14, 0.13, 0.14, 0.12)
)

ggplot(loyalty, aes(x = trust, y = mean, fill = familiarity)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .7), width = .6, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
                position = position_dodge(width = .7), width = .15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey35", "grey80")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  labs(x = "Trust in the influencer", y = "Brand loyalty", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# General Discussion

The findings indicate that influencers can strengthen brand loyalty among
millennial consumers and that familiar brands benefit the most.
